output.title: Gridframe — Layout-First Design Tool
output.tagline: Sketch frames. Export real CSS Grid. Zero absolute positioning.
output.description_short: Gridframe (alpha) turns rough wireframes into responsive CSS Grid and Flexbox — with a layout audit that catches overflow bugs before engineering ever sees the design.
output.description_long:
**Gridframe is in private alpha.** Join the waitlist to get early access.

Most design-to-code tools export absolutely-positioned rectangles. Engineers throw them away and rebuild every layout from scratch. Responsive bugs surface at handoff. Sprints slip.

Gridframe works differently. You sketch rough frames on a **layout-first canvas** — structure is the primitive, not rectangles. Gridframe resolves your frames into a proper responsive grid system with real breakpoints, then exports **clean CSS Grid and Flexbox** that engineers will actually keep.

Before handoff, the built-in **layout audit** scans your design for overflow errors and breakpoint bugs. In alpha testing it caught **140 overflow bugs** across users' production sites — problems that would have landed in the sprint backlog instead.

Exported CSS passes stylelint with zero warnings, as shown in the published demo repos.

**Who it's for:** Product designers and design engineers at startups where handoff friction burns sprint time — especially during responsive redesigns or design-system builds.

3,400 designers are already on the waitlist. If layout handoff keeps eating your sprints, Gridframe was built for you.
keywords: design to code no absolute positioning
screenshot_order: 1st — Layout canvas showing a rough wireframe being resolved into a responsive grid system: proves the core thesis instantly and shows the layout-first primitive in action.
2nd — Layout audit panel listing overflow and breakpoint bugs caught before handoff: makes the 140-bug proof point tangible and answers the 'what does it actually do' question.
3rd — Exported CSS Grid code side-by-side with the design, stylelint output showing zero warnings: closes the loop for design engineers and proves the output is production-ready.

faq.a: Gridframe is in private alpha. You can join the waitlist and we'll invite you in batches as we open access.

faq.q: How is this different from exporting CSS from Figma?
faq.a: Figma exports absolute positioning. Gridframe exports real CSS Grid and Flexbox with responsive breakpoints — code engineers keep rather than rewrite.

faq.q: Does it import my existing Figma files?
faq.a: Figma import is on the roadmap but not yet available in alpha. Gridframe currently works from its own layout-first canvas.

faq.q: Will the exported CSS work with our existing codebase?
faq.a: Exported CSS passes stylelint with zero warnings and uses standard Grid and Flexbox — no proprietary runtime or wrapper required.

faq.q: What does the layout audit actually check?
faq.a: It scans for overflow errors and breakpoint bugs before handoff. In alpha it caught 140 such bugs across users' production sites.

output.cta: Join the waitlist — get early access to Gridframe alpha.
